concepts.definition: An upward (minus) y speed given to the hero all at once.
concepts.example: set kahraman speed x (x speed) y -250 launches the hero upwards.
concepts.pitfall: Typing a positive number: the hero goes down instead of up.

concepts.definition: The moment the hero is at its highest, when gravity has brought the upward speed down to zero.
concepts.example: If the speed is -260 and the acceleration 520, it reaches the top in 0.5 seconds.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking the jump ends at the top; gravity brings the hero back down.

concepts.definition: The `touching a wall below?` block tells you whether there is a wall under the hero.
concepts.example: It is true on the ground and false in the air.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting this condition: the hero jumps in the air too, in other words it flies.

concepts.definition: Putting the jump block inside `if on the ground`.
concepts.example: When the A button is pressed, the speed block runs if it is touching a wall below.
concepts.pitfall: Putting the jump inside when game starts: it only happens once, at the start.

concepts.definition: Putting the hero's own x speed in the x speed slot when jumping.
concepts.example: The `kahraman x speed` block keeps the walking direction during the jump.
concepts.pitfall: Typing 0 for the x speed: the hero goes straight up and straight down.

concepts.definition: How big the jump speed is; the height grows with the square of the speed.
concepts.example: Going from -250 to -300 raises the rise from 60 pixels to about 86 pixels.
concepts.pitfall: Raising the speed too much: the hero can leave the screen, and the platforms lose their point.

quiz.prompt: Why is a minus number typed for the y speed to jump?
options: Because on the screen y grows downwards, so up is minus
Because the A button needs a minus value
Because gravity works with a minus number
quiz.explanation: Because y grows downwards on the screen, the upward direction is minus. A positive number pushes the hero down. The "sound" or "key" reasons among the options have nothing to do with the sign of the speed.

quiz.prompt: The hero jumps with a y speed of -260, and the gravity acceleration is 520 pixels/s². In how many seconds does its upward speed drop to zero and reach the highest point?
quiz.explanation: Time = speed / acceleration = 260 / 520 = 0.5 seconds. The speed goes down by 520 every second; it takes half a second for 260 to drop to zero. Because the engine works in steps of 1/60 of a second, a difference of 0.05 seconds is accepted.

quiz.prompt:
While in the air, the player presses A again and again. How does this program move the hero?

```
when A button is pressed:
  set kahraman speed x (kahraman x speed) y -250
```
options: Presses in the air do nothing
It shoots up again on every press and jumps in the air too
The hero sinks into the ground
It only jumps on the first press
quiz.explanation: There is no condition in the block asking whether it is on the ground. On every press the upward speed is set to -250 again, so the hero shoots up in the air too and rises as much as you like. The fix is to put this block inside `if is kahraman touching a wall below? do`.

quiz.prompt:
When you press A, the hero is pushed towards the ground instead of jumping. Which line is wrong?

```
1  when A button is pressed:
2    if is kahraman touching a wall below? do:
3      set kahraman speed x (kahraman x speed) y 250
4      play melody [jump]
```
options: Line 1: the A button event is wrong
Line 3: the sign of the y speed is wrong
quiz.explanation: On line 3 the y speed is written as positive; positive y means down. To jump up it should be -250. The condition on line 2 is correct, and the sound on line 4 does not affect the jump.

quiz.prompt: To make the hero keep going in the direction it was walking while it jumps, what should go in the x speed slot of the speed block?
quiz.explanation: When the hero's own `x speed` block is used, the sideways speed is kept as it was at the moment of the jump. If 0 is typed, the hero goes straight up and down; if 70 is typed, the hero shoots off to the right even when it was standing still.
